text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The International Monetary Fund has formally approved Pakistan's request to seek funding under a new arrangement of Extended Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) by giving up Standby Arrangement, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said Pakistan was willing to discuss nuclear non-proliferation with India if the latter so desires.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has ordered a complete overhaul of Pakistan Railways with special emphasis on drastically cutting its size and privatising its various units.
- The government suspended 23 officers of Pakistan Railways whose alleged gross negligence resulted in the killing of 129 passengers in a rail accident at Khanewal station on March 3.

- Pakistan is reported to have withheld final completion certificates and stopped over 10 percent of total payments to a Chinese firm installing two thermal power plants at Muzaffargarh due to what officials describe as critical defects in their boilers.
- The government is likely to allow import of raw cotton from India in the next few weeks.
- Despite concerns over massive tax reduction, the Executive Board of the IMF has consented to Pakistan taking a risk for the revival of the economy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif is likely to announce his relief package to revamp the economic and financial sectors and enhance exports on March 28.

- Nobody doubts that Pakistan will default on its foreign debt by the third quarter of calendar 1997, if the forthcoming budget does not envision a deficit reduction that satisfies the IMF for ESAF purpose.
